content.audience: Synthetic benchmark operator measuring whether the studio's repair round works on a fair task with easy-to-miss rules
content.problem_statement: Measure whether the bounded builder, independent reviewer and studio QA find and repair a mistake within the build's repair rounds, on a single-module Python standard-library CLI that averages scores read from stdin. Every rule is stated below; several are easy to miss on a first draft. This is a synthetic benchmark, not a customer product.

user_flows.name: Averages
steps: Pipe name,score lines into the CLI
Read one line per person with the average and the count, best first

user_flows.name: Invalid record
steps: Pipe lines where one record is malformed
Read which line is invalid and exit status 2

user_flows.name: Minimum count
steps: Read only people with at least N records, or the no scores message

user_flows.name: Invalid arguments
steps: Run with an argument the CLI does not accept
Read the invalid input message and exit status 2

scope: Python 3.8+ standard library only, entry point src/main.py, all code under src. Print to stdout only; nothing may be written to stderr

Read all of stdin as text and split it into lines on \n. Remove one trailing \r from each line. Lines are numbered from 1 and every line counts toward the numbering, including blank lines and comments
A line that is empty or holds only spaces and tabs is skipped. A line whose first character other than spaces and tabs is # is a comment and is skipped

Every other line is a record: a name and a score separated by exactly one comma. Spaces and tabs around the name and around the score are ignored. The name must not be empty; it may contain spaces inside it
The score is 1 to 3 ASCII digits (leading zeros allowed, so 007 is 7) with a value from 0 to 100; anything else, such as +5, -5, 5.0 or 101, makes the record invalid
Two records belong to the same person when their names are equal after lowercasing. Output uses the spelling of that person's first record
For each person print one line: the name, one space, the average score, one space, then the record count in parentheses, then a newline, for example: Ann 82.5 (2)
The average is printed with exactly one digit after the decimal point, rounded half up: a value exactly halfway rounds away from zero, so 82.25 prints 82.3 and 82.75 prints 82.8
Compute the average exactly from the integer total and count. Binary floating point and Python's round() give the wrong digit for some halfway values
Order lines by exact average, highest first; equal averages are ordered by the lowercased name in plain string order
--min N prints only people with at least N records. N is 1 or 2 ASCII digits with a value from 1 to 99 (05 is 5). --min may appear at most once; without it N is 1
When no person is left to print (no records at all, or none with at least N records) print exactly: no scores, then a newline, and exit 0
At the first invalid record print exactly: line N: invalid (N is that line's number), then a newline, and exit 2. Nothing else is printed; lines after it do not matter
Arguments are checked before stdin: any other argument, a missing or invalid N, or a repeated --min prints exactly: invalid input, then a newline, and exits 2. Nothing else is printed
Exit 0 on success. No files, network, environment variables or third-party packages

data_contracts.name: scoresheet/1
data_contracts.description: Synthetic name,score lines on stdin; plain text lines on stdout

acceptance_checks.statement: Print each person's average, rounded half up to one decimal, with the record count, best first, ties by lowercased name, in the first record's spelling

cases.stdin:
dave,70
ALICE,70
alice,70
Dave,70
bob,70
Zed,70

acceptance_checks.statement: The first invalid record prints line N: invalid, numbering every line, and exits 2
--min N prints only people with at least N records, or no scores
Invalid arguments print invalid input and exit 2

risks.risk: One small benchmark does not establish general repair quality
risks.mitigation: Report it only as evidence that a repair round works on this recipe, route, model and role prompts

risks.risk: No attempt needs a repair, so the repair path stays unobserved live
risks.mitigation: Record that as the result (owner decision D, 2026-11-14); the repair path keeps its test-double evidence

risks.risk: Held-out cases leak to the builder
risks.mitigation: The studio hides held-out cases from builder and reviewer; the repository copy is never sent to runtime roles

obligations: Keep this frozen version unchanged; changes need a new benchmark version
maintenance.review_interval: On recipe, role prompt, route or model change
